# Consuming APIs

Read before implementing an HTTP/SDK client, sync job, or another service integration.

## Client boundary

- Centralize base URL, authentication, finite timeouts, concurrency, retry policy, serialization, and
  telemetry in one typed client. Reuse connection/session objects according to the library lifecycle.
- Parse responses into your own boundary models. Treat missing/partial/empty results as data, never
  forward raw upstream errors, and keep upstream content in a schema- and size-bounded data field if
  an LLM will consume it.
- Cache and refresh expiring credentials according to the provider contract; do not authenticate on
  every request or expose tokens in URLs, flags, logs, or errors.
- Follow provider pagination/continuation until the task's explicit bound, streaming or batching
  rather than loading an unlimited result set.

## Failure policy

- Retry only documented transient failures that are safe to repeat. Bound attempts, elapsed time,
  concurrency, backoff, and jitter; honor `Retry-After`.
- Do not blindly retry a write. Use the provider's idempotency mechanism or a local operation record
  that handles concurrent duplicates and unknown outcomes.
- A circuit breaker is optional policy, not a universal requirement. Use one when measured persistent
  failure and call volume justify fast failure; define half-open recovery and fallback behavior.
- Check current state before a write and separate decision from effect. Production writes still require
  the repository's effect-bound human approval and executor.

## Evidence

Emit approved target/operation, latency, outcome class, attempt, and correlation metrics without
sensitive payloads. Propagate only supported tracing/correlation fields. Test timeout, retryable and
terminal failures, rate limiting, malformed responses, pagination bounds, credential refresh, and
unknown write outcome.
